title: ambuild streaming — bounded-memory IVF build

methodology.peak: kernel VmHWM (high-water anon-rss) of the CREATE INDEX backend, sampled every 0.3s + read at completion
methodology.runs_note: N=1; VmHWM is a deterministic high-water of the allocation path (low variance) -> defensible for peak-RSS without >=3 runs; build_s is single-run/indicative, NOT the DoD metric (DoD is peak ratio)

dataset.note: synthetic clustered; the build MEMORY peak is dataset-independent of recall — this measures build RSS, not recall

correctness.note: v5/v6 scan==seqscan suites exercise the streaming writers -> byte-correct pages; build_owned asserted byte-identical to build; no magic bump -> no REINDEX

findings.dod_met: 30M build completes on a 64GB box at 1.28x (v5) / 1.50x (v6) base; pre-M89 OOM'd at 4.21x (reproduces M88)
findings.increment1_insufficient_measured: clone-elimination alone re-measured at 4.21x OOM -> the list_entries() clone + writers' enc_vec/items buffering were the dominant copies; streaming page-writes (Increment 2) is what bounded the peak
findings.sq8_size: v6/SQ8 index 3.36x smaller than v5/f32 (15GB vs 4.46GB) -- confirms M85/M88

caveats: plan specified Postgres tuplesort FFI (Option B); implementation achieved the DoD with clone-elimination + streaming page-writes (no FFI) at lower risk -- tuplesort was YAGNI for 30M (parsimony deviation, ADR-0039)
NOT O(maintenance_work_mem): peak still carries the 1x idx.vectors copy (~15.4GB) -> 100M (~51GB base) still won't fit commodity RAM; true tuplesort vector-streaming is the 100M+ follow-up
v6/SQ8 at the 1.50x boundary (sq8_codes ~3.8GB buffered); streaming sq8 per-list would lower it, not needed for DoD
v3/v4 interleaved (non-storage-separated) build paths unchanged -- legacy/non-DoD, still OOM at billion-scale
